newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn to start oil sale in coming weeks -source.
newsitem.headline: Bonn to start oil sale in coming weeks -source.

text.p: German government sources said on Friday Bonn planned to sell 2.8 million barrels of crude oil in the next few weeks, the first tranche in the planned sale of its entire strategic reserves of 7.3 million tonnes.
Sources said the government planned to sell 450,000 cubic metres of oil -- equivalent to 2.8 million barrels -- in the first tranche of the sale, which it expects to complete by the end of 1999.

The source said 45 percent of Bonn's reserves was heavy crude with an average gravity of 30.5 API, including Iranian heavy, Arab heavy and Arab light. The rest included oil from the Gulf, the North Sea and West Africa, he said.

The option of oil sales was first mooted by Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt last month. Government sources on Thursday confirmed Germany planned to sell 400 million marks of crude this year to help fill a yawning budget gap and aid its bid to qualify for Europe's single currency.
Rexrodt said then the sale of the entire reserves would raise around 1.4 billion marks. The source said Bonn had yet to decide what portion of the reserves would be sold in each year.
